reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable space and canonical Lebesgue measure dx; dimension zero is allowed, and the approved ambient instances are part of the contract. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume x->exp(-W(x)) is Lebesgue integrable. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), namely exp(-W)/integral exp(-W) times volume; positivity of its normalizing integral is not built into the definition.
For every real-linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E), assume D is closable and has exactly the following graph: for every a in L2(mu;R) and H in L2(mu;E), (a,H) belongs to graph(D) if and only if there exists a smooth compactly supported phi:E->R with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) mu-almost everywhere. The closure is the same operator defined by the topological graph closure, on its submodule domain.
For every real epsilon>0 and every scalar L2 input f for this same D, there exists u in domain(D.closure) satisfying the following simultaneous conclusions. Write u_rep and f_rep for the standard measurable representatives of the actual scalar L2 classes, and G_rep for the standard representative of G=D.closure(u) in the actual vector L2 quotient. In the formulas below set r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x); this notation abbreviates the exact displayed expression.
(1) For every v in domain(D.closure),
  epsilon*<u,v>_{L2(mu;R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(v)>_{L2(mu;E)}=<f,v>_{L2(mu;R)}.
(2) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to canonical Lebesgue volume.
(3) For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every direction v in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) dx.
(4) x->||r(x)||^2 is locally Lebesgue integrable, with the real scalar norm in this squared expression.
(5) For every compact set K contained in E, u_rep, G_rep, and r each satisfy MemLp with exponent 2 and the actual restricted measure volume.restrict K. Each assertion includes a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm with respect to that restricted measure.
(6) For every C2 compactly supported phi:E->R, both x->u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) and x->r(x)*phi(x) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) dx = integral r(x)*phi(x) dx.
Here the test-function Laplacian is the actual finite-basis trace of its derivative. The distribution equation tests u_rep against this C2 test Laplacian; it makes no pointwise total-Laplacian assertion about u_rep. The Hilbert variational inner products use mu, while all local integrability and distribution integrals use canonical Lebesgue volume. One u and its actual output G serve all variational v, all C1 directional tests, every compact K, and all C2 distribution tests.
The operator D is quantified before epsilon and f and works for all their permitted values. Its density or existence is not an additional premise or an existential conclusion of this universal implication. The exact forcing expression is epsilon*u_rep+<gradient(W),G_rep>-f_rep. There is no mean-zero restriction on f, no C2 assumption on W, and no classical differentiability or H2 regularity conclusion for u_rep. The statement asserts existence of such u, without a uniqueness, quantitative bound, or jointly measurable selection conclusion.
objects: C1 real potential W with volume-integrable exp(-W); normalized tilt mu; universal scalar-to-vector actual L2 partial operator D, its exact smooth compact-support gradient graph and closure; positive real epsilon; scalar L2 forcing f; closure-domain solution u and actual closure output G; real residual r; C1 directional tests, compact subsets K, and C2 Laplacian distribution tests.
domains: E is finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel, including dimension zero, with canonical volume. Scalar and vector Lp classes at exponent 2 are the actual quotient spaces and their coercions are the standard measurable representatives. D is a real-linear partial operator with a submodule domain; u and the variational v are elements of D.closure.domain; G=D.closure u lies in the actual vector L2 quotient. All local integrability, unannotated Integrable and integral expressions use volume. All compact restrictions explicitly use volume.restrict K. Ordinary directional v lies in E. C1/C2 test functions are real valued and compact topological support; graph generators are smooth compactly supported. Laplacian.laplacian phi is the actual finite-basis trace on the C2 test phi, not a Laplacian applied to arbitrary L2 u. Here both L2 quotients and Hilbert inner products use mu=volume.tilted(-W).
quantifiers: Universally over the approved ambient E instances and W satisfying C1 and exp(-W) integrability. After let mu, forall D, then D.IsClosable and the universal graph-iff premises. Graph characterization is forall a,H with exists smooth compact-support phi. Then forall epsilon:R, epsilon>0 -> forall f:scalar L2(mu), exists u:D.closure.domain. This u precedes forall variational v; the ordinary weak-gradient block forall psi with C1 and compact-support antecedents then forall direction v:E; forall compact K via IsCompact K antecedent; and forall C2 compact-support phi for the final distribution block. The epsilon/f choices do not change D; tests and K do not change u.
assumptions: Approved section ambient finite-dimensional real inner-product/Borel/volume structure, permitting dimension zero. W is C1 and exp(-W) is Lebesgue integrable. The universal D is closable and its graph is exactly the smooth compact-support function/gradient pairs modulo mu null sets. epsilon is any strictly positive real; f has only actual scalar L2(mu) membership. No dense-domain premise, no probability or positive-normalization premise, no mean-zero f, no W C2 premise, and no added u regularity premise.
conclusion: For every positive epsilon and every actual scalar L2 f, exists one u in closure-domain satisfying all: universal Hilbert variational equation; local volume integrability of scalar u_rep and vector G_rep; for every C1 compact-support psi and v:E both ordinary weak-gradient products are volume-integrable and integral psi*<G_rep,v>=-integral u_rep*Dpsi[v]; local volume integrability of ||r||^2; for every compact K all three actual MemLp 2 (volume.restrict K) assertions for u_rep,G_rep,r; for every C2 compact-support phi both u_rep*Laplacian(phi) and r*phi are volume-integrable and their integrals are equal. r is exactly epsilon*u_rep+<gradient of the stated potential,G_rep>-f_rep. All use the same selected u and actual G, not independently chosen representative outputs. This is a universal implication for every closable D with the exact graph, not an assertion that such a D exists. r uses gradient W.
scopes: mu is the actual exp(-W)/partition-volume tilt. D is fixed before all epsilon,f. Every selected u/G satisfies every conjunct; r is an abbreviation of the displayed scalar expression, not another existential object. Graph representative equalities are mu-a.e.; local and distribution conclusions concern the standard actual representatives and volume. MemLp on every compact restriction includes actual measurability and finite norm. The ordinary distribution equation has positive sign integral u*Delta(phi)=integral r*phi; the weak-gradient equation has a minus sign. No pointwise Delta u, classical second derivatives, H2 regularity, core/density conclusion, uniqueness, energy estimate, or measurable solution-selection assertion.
constant_dependencies: No unspecified bound constant. epsilon is any strictly positive real. mu depends on W and volume; a permitted D is supplied before epsilon/f. u may depend on W,D,epsilon,f; G is exactly closureD(u), and r has exact coefficients +epsilon,+1,-1 in epsilon*u+<gradient W,G>-f. Compact K and all tests/directions are universal after u. Exponent is exactly 2 and the locally integrated real norm is squared.
